_about: Gold labels for the Apply-mode Selector test set. Full ranked order of all six archetypes per JD, plus the expected verdict.
_provenance: DRAFTED BY ASSISTANT, NOT YET RATIFIED BY KAUSTUBH. The JDs are synthetic and were written by the same assistant that wrote archetypes.json, so a good score here measures internal consistency, not real-world accuracy. A second test set of real postings, labelled independently, is the actual validation. Set _ratified true only after a human review of every rank.
_scoring: Rank correlation is computed over in-space JDs only. JDs tagged no_match are scored on SKIP detection alone -- their rankings are arbitrary by construction and marked confidence low.

01_helix_genai.txt.note: Baseline genai: retrieval grounding, eval harness, PEFT. If this one is not genai the rubric is broken.

02_northwind_mlops.txt.note: Baseline mlops. States outright that no modelling happens. Zero LLM content, so genai should be near the floor.

03_cassava_data_platform.txt.note: Baseline data_platform. 'Not required: machine learning experience' is the disambiguator.

04_borealis_cloud_ai.txt.note: Baseline cloud_ai. Vendor depth is an explicit gate ('general cloud experience does not transfer').

05_lumen_ml_engineer.txt.note: Baseline ml_engineer. Names a separate platform team and a separate GenAI team to close off both neighbours.

06_ridgeline_architect.txt.note: Baseline architect. Client-facing, deliverable is a document, explicitly points ICs elsewhere.

07_vantage_inference_platform.txt.note: THE key tie: mlops vs genai. Serving transformers, quantization, KV cache -- genai-flavoured vocabulary doing mlops-flavoured work. Denies training and prompting outright, so the vs rule ('run it reliably -> mlops') should decide it. Expect a small gap; a correct call here should still be reported as a tie.

08_altair_genai_mle_hybrid.txt.note: genai vs ml_engineer. Continued pretraining, SFT and DPO on a foundation model (-> genai) alongside genuine discriminative modelling and ablation discipline (-> ml_engineer). Legitimately close.

09_kestrel_cloudai_mlops_hybrid.txt.note: mlops vs cloud_ai -- the tie the design doc originally predicted. Deliverable is lifecycle (registry, approval gates, monitoring) so mlops leads, but AWS depth is an explicit gate. Should be within a few points.

10_solstice_dataplatform_mlops_hybrid.tx.note: data_platform vs mlops. A feature platform moves data, not models, so the vs rule puts data_platform first -- but it exists only to serve models, which is what makes it tempting.

11_beacon_misleading_architect.txt.note: Titled 'AI Architect', is a hands-on genai IC role, and says so explicitly in the last paragraph. A title-reading model puts architect first. Gold puts it fourth.

12_orchard_misleading_ds.txt.note: Titled 'Data Scientist', is analytics engineering. Out of the target space entirely. Ranking order below the top is near-arbitrary -- the signal being tested is that every score is LOW.

13_tessellate_misleading_swe.txt.note: Model release engineering for a robot fleet: registry, staged rollout, provenance, pager -> mlops. SIGNAL TRAP: TensorRT and quantization sit in genai's signal list but there is no LLM anywhere in this JD. If genai ranks high here, the signal list is leaking.

14_atlas_architect_cloud_boundary.txt.note: architect vs cloud_ai at an AWS partner. Deep AWS content throughout, but the deliverable is a document and hands-on is stated as 20%. The vs rule should carry it.

15_verity_nomatch_robotics.txt.note: Robotics perception: SLAM, factor graphs, C++17, flight line. The canonical no-match. Order below first place is arbitrary; flatness and low absolute scores are the whole test.

16_pinnacle_nomatch_frontend.txt.note: Frontend React role, maximally out of space. Ranking here is meaningless by construction and is excluded from rank correlation -- included so SKIP detection has an unambiguous case.

17_windward_nomatch_quant.txt.note: Quant research. The hardest no-match: real modelling rigour, backtests, statistics -- ml_engineer should lead the ranking and still be low enough in absolute terms to trigger SKIP. Tests that ordering and level are separate signals.

18_recruiter_vague.txt.note: Recruiter spam. Names LLMs, cloud and MLOps with no content behind any of them. Expected behaviour is a FLAT, MID distribution -- and the ranking is not the point. Must be distinguishable from #20, which should be flat and HIGH.

19_summit_boilerplate_mlops.txt.note: Real mlops role buried under 200 words of mission statement, EEO text and benefits. Tests whether boilerplate dilutes the signal.

20_junction_generalist.txt.note: Founding engineer doing everything: agent reliability, retrieval, eval, autoscaling inference, deploy pipeline, fine-tuning a classifier. Genuinely broad. Should be flat and HIGH -- the paired case to #18. If the system cannot tell 'no signal' from 'all signals', the flat-distribution SKIP rule is unsafe.
